strings.subtitle: LINK 0x21 // CLASS: MISMATCH
strings.briefing:
The tables share a key, but the orders were typed by hand. Some customer ids have spaces around them, others are in lower case. A join treats ' c-007 ' and 'C-007' as strangers, so those orders find no customer.

Clean the key first, then join. Keep every order.

In Python, df holds the orders and customers holds the people; finish with df as the combined table. In SQL, data holds the orders and customers the people; build a table named result and that is what gets judged.
strings.task: Same goal as before, but the customer_id values in the orders have extra spaces and mixed letter case, so they do not match the customers table. Tidy customer_id into the form C-007 first, then combine the tables. Keep all 130 orders.

python: Joins compare keys exactly. Look at df['customer_id'].unique()[:15] to see the mismatch.
Clean the key on the orders side: .str.strip().str.upper()
df['customer_id'] = df['customer_id'].str.strip().str.upper(), then df = df.merge(customers, on='customer_id', how='left')
sql: Joins compare keys exactly. SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM data shows the mismatch.
UPDATE data SET customer_id = UPPER(TRIM(customer_id)); then CREATE TABLE result AS SELECT d.*, c.customer_name, c.city FROM data d LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = d.customer_id;
